edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina (PL 2, Paris 1844), Adversus Marcionem, liber III, via Latin Wikisource transcription
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Imo, inquis, spero ab illo quod et ipsum faciat ad testimonium diversitatis regnum Dei aeternae et coelestis possessionis. Caeterum, vester Christus pristimum statum Judaeis pollicetur, ex restitutione terrae, et post decursum vitae, apud inferos in sinu Abrahae refrigerium. Deum optimum! si reddit placatus, quod et abstulerat iratus. O Deum tuum qui et caedit et sanat, condit mala et facit pacem! O Deum etiam ad inferos usque misericordem! Sed de sinu Abrahae suo tempore. De restitutione vero Judaeae, quam et ipsi Judaei, ita ut describitur, sperant, locorum et regionum nominibus inducti, quomodo allegorica interpretatio in Christum et in Ecclesiam, et habitum et fructum ejus spiritaliter competat, et longum est persequi, et in alio opere digestum, quod inscribimus, De spe fidelium; et in praesenti vel eo otiosum, quia non de terrena, sed de coelesti promissione sit quaestio. Nam et confitemur in terra nobis regnum repromissum; sed ante coelum, sed alio statu; utpote post resurrectionem in mille annos, in civitate divini operis Hierusalem coelo delata, quam et Apostolus matrem nostram sursum designat, et politeuma nostrum, id est, municipatum in coelis esse pronuntians, alicui utique coelesti civitati eum deputat. Hanc et Ezechiel novit, et apostolus Joannes vidit, et qui apud fidem nostram est, novae prophetiae sermo testatur, ut etiam effigiem civitatis ante repraesentationem ejus conspectu futuram in signum praedicarit. Denique proxime expunctum est orientali expeditione. Constat enim, ethnicis quoque testibus, in Judaea per dies quadraginta matutinis momentis civitatem de coelo pependisse, omni meoniorum habitu evanescente de profectu diei, et alias de proximo nullam. Hanc dicimus excipiendis resurrectione sanctis, et refovendis omnium bonorum utique spiritalium copia in compensationem eorum quae in saeculo vel despeximus, vel amisimus, a Deo prospectam. Siquidem et justum, et Deo dignum, illic quoque exultare famulos ejus, ubi sunt et afflicti in nomine ipsius. Haec ratio regni terreni, post cujus mille annos, intra quam aetatem concluditur sanctorum resurrectio, pro meritis maturius vel tardius resurgentium, tunc et mundi destructione, et judicii conflagratione commissa, demutati in atomo in angelicam substantiam, scilicet per illud incorruptelae superindumentum, transferemur in coeleste regnum, de quo nunc sic ideo retractatur, quasi non praedicato apud Creatorem, ac per hoc, alterius Dei Christum probante, a quo primo et solo sit revelatum.
pass_a_gloss: Indeed, you ask, I hope from Him what also He Himself does for a testimony of the diversity of the kingdom of God, of eternal and heavenly possession. Moreover, your Christ first promises to the Jews a former state, from the restitution of the earth, and after the course of life, in the underworld, in the bosom of Abraham, refreshment. Good God, if He returns what He had taken away, placated, having been angry. Oh God of yours, who both kills and heals, founds evils and makes peace. Oh God, even merciful to the underworld. But concerning the bosom of Abraham, in its own time. Indeed, about the restitution of Judea, which also the Jews themselves hope for, as it is described, induced by names of places and regions, how an allegorical interpretation into Christ and into the Church, and its habit and fruit, spiritually competes, and it is long to pursue, and in another work digested, which we entitle, On the Hope of the Faithful, and in the present, or even idle, because the question is not about an earthly, but about a heavenly promise. For we also confess that the kingdom is promised to us on earth, but before heaven, but in another state, as it were, after the resurrection, in a thousand years, in the city of the divine work, Jerusalem, lifted up to heaven, which also the Apostle designates as our mother above, and our community, that is, our municipality in the heavens, pronouncing it to be in a certain heavenly city. This city also Ezekiel knows, and the Apostle John saw, and the word of the new prophecy testifies, which even predicts the image of the city before its representation, as a sign to come. Finally, recently it has been confirmed by an eastern expedition. For it is established, even by pagan witnesses, that in Judea, for forty days, at morning moments, a city hung from heaven, with every cloud-like appearance vanishing at the progress of the day, and at other times, none at all. We say this city is for receiving the resurrection of the saints, and for renewing all spiritual goods, certainly, in compensation for those things which we either despised or lost in the world, foreseen by God. Since it is also just and worthy of God, that there His servants should also rejoice, where they are afflicted in His name. This reason of the earthly kingdom, after whose thousand years, within which age the resurrection of the saints is concluded, according to the merits, sooner or later, of the resurgent, then also, with the destruction of the world and the conflagration of judgment committed, changed into an atom, into an angelic substance, certainly, through that superindumentum of incorruptibility, we shall be transferred into the heavenly kingdom, about which now it is thus retracted, as if it had not been predicted by the Creator, and through this, proving Christ of another God, from whom alone it was first and only revealed.
pass_b_english: "Indeed," you ask, "I hope from Him that He Himself also acts as a testimony to the diversity of the kingdom of God, of eternal and heavenly possession." Moreover, your Christ promises the Jews a former state through the restitution of the earth, and after the course of life, refreshment in the underworld in the bosom of Abraham (Luke 16:22-23). Good God! If He returns what He took away in anger, now that He is placated. Oh, your God who both kills and heals, who founds evils and makes peace! Oh God, merciful even to the underworld! But we will discuss the bosom of Abraham at its proper time. Regarding the restitution of Judea, which the Jews themselves also hope for exactly as it is described, they are induced by the names of places and regions to pursue an allegorical interpretation of how it spiritually applies to Christ and the Church, its habit and fruit; that is a long pursuit, and it is digested in another work which we title *On the Hope of the Faithful*, and it is idle even for the present, because the question concerns not an earthly but a heavenly promise. For we also confess that a kingdom is promised to us on earth, but before heaven, and in another state—namely, after the resurrection, for a thousand years in the city of the divine work, Jerusalem, lifted up to heaven. The Apostle designates this city as our mother above (Galatians 4:26), and pronounces our community, that is, our municipality, to be in the heavens (Philippians 3:20), assigning it to a certain heavenly city. Ezekiel also knows this city (Ezekiel 40-48), and the Apostle John saw it (Revelation 21:1-22:5), and the word of the new prophecy which is with our faith testifies to it, even predicting the image of the city before its representation as a sign to come. Finally, this was recently confirmed by an eastern expedition. For it is established, even by pagan witnesses, that in Judea for forty days at morning moments a city hung from heaven, every cloud-like appearance vanishing at the progress of the day, and at other times none at all. We say this city is for receiving the resurrection of the saints, and for renewing the full abundance of all spiritual goods in compensation for those things which in the world we either despised or lost, foreseen by God. Since it is also just and worthy of God that His servants should rejoice there, where they are afflicted in His name. This is the rationale of the earthly kingdom: after its thousand years, within which age the resurrection of the saints is concluded, according to the merits, sooner or later, of those rising, then also with the destruction of the world and the conflagration of judgment committed, we shall be changed in an atom into an angelic substance, certainly through that superindumentum of incorruptibility, and transferred into the heavenly kingdom. This kingdom is now so retracted as if it had not been predicted by the Creator, and through this, proving Christ to be of another God, from whom alone it was first and only revealed.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex theological arguments regarding the earthly and heavenly kingdoms, the millennial period, and the nature of the resurrection. Pass A provides a faithful literal rendering, while Pass B provides a more fluent version with necessary scriptural identifications for the allusions (Luke 16:22-23, Galatians 4:26, Philippians 3:20, Ezekiel 40-48, Revelation 21:1-22:5). All clauses, including the specific description of the 'city hanging from heaven' and the 'superindumentum of incorruptibility', are preserved.
